tagline: A 360M model pretrained from scratch to write its own search queries

scenes.narration: Day 57: QueryLM, a 360 million parameter model pretrained from scratch to write search queries, tested on a local CPU.

scenes.heading: What is it?
bullets: Pretrained on Wikipedia text with inline search blocks
Learns to write a query, not to predict the retrieved passage
Paired with a compute-matched baseline with no search
scenes.narration: QueryLM was pretrained on Wikipedia text where some positions were replaced with a search query followed by a retrieved passage. The model only learned to write the query, never to predict the passage itself.

steps.narration: Given a question, the model can open a search block and write its own query, at most 24 tokens.
The caller runs any retriever and inserts the passage back into the text. The model was never trained to generate that passage itself.
With the passage in context, the model keeps generating and answers the question.

scenes.heading: What we found
scenes.caption: QueryLM's correct answers out of 8 questions: 3 with search disabled, only 2 once it searched. The standard no-search baseline scored 0 out of 8.
lines: no search : Jane Austen, Mount Everest
scenes.narration: On 8 knowledge questions, QueryLM beat the standard baseline 3 to 0 even without searching. But letting it actually search sometimes backfired: two answers it had right turned into an empty string or an unrelated word.
Chat fine-tuning fixed this instability. Full results and sources are in the Zenn article, linked below.
